posts.name: TheNovaKid
posts.cooked:
Big thanks to mistdrake for pointing this out and actually coming up with this idea, this wasn't on me at all -

 

PA Captain Cosmic, Guise, Rouge K.N.Y.F.E, and The Sentinals vs Heroic Infinitor

Field's full of Manifestations and we're all running low on health.  Infinitor's got about 8 HP left and we're getting worried.  The Sentinals get their turn and I play Blackout - allowing the Writhe to hit someone for damage, who then can hit everyone for Infernal.

Mistdrake stops me and tells me to hit Infinitor.

I ask, "Why?"

They do the math and say that Infinitor will hit every one of his manifestations and I laugh it off, but follow their logic anyway.

Few seconds later we're both sitting in front of a success screen, with Infinitor having won by dealing all his manifestations - thereby killing them - with infernal damage.

 

So lesson learned, you can punch Infinitor and still win.

It's one of the stupidest things I have ever heard of and it's very, very alarming and I'm sure Nigel doesn't deserve it at all but hey if you lose your paitence with him

there's that.

Even if this was discovered before this still has me laughing because I didn't know it worked this way and I'm giggling.

 

Poor Infinitor.

posts.name: WarrenAC
posts.cooked:
Blackout in general is great on heroes that have a lot of general (not damage-type specific) damage bonuses. You trade one a single hit to that hero for hits to all the non-hero targets - its like a general-purpose version of Bunker's External Combustion.  Setback (High Risk Behaviour), Chrono-Ranger (Hunter and Hunted), Mr. Fixer (Bloody Knuckles, Styles and Tools) and Termi-Nation Absolute Zero (Shivers) can have big boosts to damage dealt (and received, so be careful - they have to survive the hit!).  Argent Adept can also boost damage,  and more globally Legacy and Ra.

Mr. Fixer also has bonuses from style (Grease Monkey Fist)/tool (Wrench or Dual for +1 damage, or Hoist to reduce enemy damage)/harmony (+1)

Note that if you have Twist the Ether on the hero you can manipulate the outgoing damage type and increase damage as well.

The only caveat is that Writhe has to actually deal damage,  so while you could mitigate some of the damage, you also need to be sure you do at least 1 point of damage otherwise the area hit won't happen. Also,  you must attack all the non-hero targets,  so if you're trying to not explode an explosives wagon or keep around a non-hero target you need to be careful.

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
How does that Blackout trick work with Mr. Fixer and either the Dual Crowbars or the Jack Handle?  

 

Ex 1: Say there are 5 non-hero targets, and Fixer has the Jack Handle out.  Writhe targets Fixer with Blackout.  By the terms of Blackout, Fixer would now deal 2 Infernal damage to each non-hero target.  But Jack Handle means that every time Fixer inflicts damage, he inflicts it on all non-hero targets.  Does that mean that Fixer now gets 5 attacks on all non-hero targets?

 

Ex: 2:  Again 5 non-hero targets out there, but this time Fixer has the Dual Crowbars.  Writhe again targets Fixer with Blackout.  Does that mean that Fixer gets 5 "initial" hits via Blackout, and 5 follow-up hits with the Dual Crowbars?

posts.cooked: Why only one extra attack?  Dual Crowbars says that "Whenever Mr. Fixer deals damage, he may deal that damage to 1 other target as well."  Similar language on Jack Handle ("Whenever Mr. Fixer would deal damage to a target, he deals that much damage to all non-hero targets.") If there are (ex:) 5 non-hero targets when Blackout is played, Fixer is "dealing damage" to each one of them with Blackout, isn't he?

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
Because of Fireside chats

When Dual Crowbars and Jack Handle are in play at the same time and Mr. Fixer deals damage, the following occurs. Mr. Fixer deals the damage to all non-hero targets (due to Jack Handle). Then once that is fully resolved, Dual Crowbars takes effect based on the damage dealt to the first target. That damage is dealt to all non-hero targets (due to Jack Handle).

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked:
It's still what I described.   

Fireside Chats:

Suppose Guise has Dual Crowbars and then uses I Can Do That Too on Sky-Scraper’s Huge card. After the first “round” of damage (to non-hero targets), Dual Crowbars causes Guise to deal as much damage as was dealt to the first non-hero target to one more target. Then, after the second “round” of damage (to hero targets), Dual Crowbars causes Guise to deal as much damage as was dealt to the first hero to one more target. (This is how Dual Crowbars interacts with Jack Handle)
